challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: I am redirecting a portion of my pipeline infrastructure budget toward the loyalty data consent audit. I will accept the loss of two planned automation sprints for the next quarter. This trade allows me to build the automated contract validation layer {requirements_reuben.first} requires without waiting for external funding. In exchange, I get to shape the enforcement logic myself, ensuring the consent checks are baked into the data ingestion tools rather than bolted on later. The promotion planning cycle will not stall because I am absorbing the cost internally. This is the only way to guarantee the legal basis is enforced at the source while keeping my deployment pipeline stable.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they will accept the loss of two planned automation sprints to fund the consent audit, which fits the definition of a trade-off where something is given up.
